extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs), state air agencies, tribal governments, small entities and their representatives, industry groups, and other stakeholders affected by EPA NSPS and emission guidelines
extracted.subtask_short: EPA NSPS and emission guideline compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and regulatory text for the EPA final rule setting New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) and Emission Guidelines for greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuel-fired electric generating units, describing statutory bases, required consultations, incorporated technical standards, small-entity analyses, reliability mechanisms, and applicability dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER) statutory factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with the statutory command of CAA section 111, the final NSPS and emission guidelines reflect the application of the BSER that, taking into account costs, energy requirements, and other statutory factors, is adequately demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BSER determinations must specifically consider costs, energy requirements, and other statutory factors and be adequately demonstrated in the rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards must be cost-effective and maintain reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: These final actions ensure that EGUs reduce their GHG emissions in a manner that is cost-effective and improve the emissions performance of the sources, consistent with the applicable CAA requirements and caselaw. EPA designed these standards and emission guidelines in a way that is compatible with the nation's overall need for a reliable supply of affordable electricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory design should balance emission reductions with cost-effectiveness and grid reliability; analyses and flexibilities should demonstrate compatibility with reliable affordable electricity supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRFA / SBAR Panel convening when small-entity impacts uncertain
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA convened a SBAR Panel because it solicited comment on policy options that, if finalized, could affect the estimate of total compliance costs and therefore the impacts on small entities. EPA issued an IRFA and solicited comment on regulatory flexibilities for small business in a supplemental proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposed options could materially affect small-entity costs, EPA should prepare an IRFA, solicit comments, and convene a SBAR Panel to obtain small entity representative recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity screening methodology (use of SBA guidelines and build-history)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA revised its small business assessment to incorporate the final SBA guidelines when performing the screening analysis to identify small businesses that have built or have planned/committed builds of combustion turbines since 2017, and treated additional entities as small based on panel feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening to identify small entities should follow SBA size standards and consider historical and planned builds (since a defined date) to determine the universe of affected small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption updates affecting small-entity cost attribution (hydrogen price)
rubrics_metrics.description: The net effect of these changes is to increase the total compliance cost attributed to small entities. The EPA additionally increased the assumed delivered hydrogen price to $1.15/kg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key cost assumptions (e.g., delivered low-GHG hydrogen price) used in small-entity impact estimates must be updated when new information warrants, and those updates may materially change estimated small-entity costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method to estimate number of small businesses impacted (cost-to-revenue comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: To estimate the number of small businesses potentially impacted by the NSPS, the EPA performed a small entity screening analysis for impacts on all affected EGUs by comparing compliance costs to historic revenues at the ultimate parent company level. EPA followed SBA size standards to determine which ultimate parent entities should be considered small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare estimated compliance costs to historic generation revenues at the ultimate parent level; use SBA size standards for entity classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of rule costs to small entities (build-share approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the costs of the rule were calculated, the costs attributed to small entities were calculated by multiplying the total costs to the share of the historical build attributed to small entities. These costs were then shared to individual entities using the ratio of their build to total small entity additions in the historical dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute aggregate costs to small entities based on their share of historical/planned builds, then apportion to individual small entities proportionally to each entity's build share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of compliance-cost-to-revenue thresholds to assess significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA assessed the economic and financial impacts of the rule using the ratio of compliance costs to the value of revenues from electricity generation, focusing in particular on entities for which this measure is greater than 1 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight entities exceeding specified ratios (e.g., >1% and >3%) of compliance cost to generation revenues as indicators of potentially significant economic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and finalization of regulatory alternatives from SBAR Panel
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the Panel recommendations and public comments, the EPA is finalizing several regulatory alternatives that could accomplish the Clean Air Act objectives while minimizing any significant economic impact of the final rule on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider SBAR Panel recommendations and public comments and may adopt regulatory alternatives to reduce economic impacts on small entities while meeting statutory objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability relief instruments (short-term emergency & reliability assurance mechanisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: The short-term reliability emergency mechanism, available for both new and existing units, is designed to provide an alternative compliance strategy during acute system emergencies. The reliability assurance mechanism will be available for existing units that intend to cease operating but, for unforeseen reasons, need to temporarily remain online to support reliability beyond the planned cease operation date; it requires an adequate showing of reliability need and applies where there is insufficient time to complete a state plan revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliability mechanisms can be used as alternative compliance strategies during emergencies or unforeseen reliability needs; EPA alone decides on extensions (FERC concurrence is not required but may inform the decision). If states incorporate these instruments into plans and they meet emission-guideline requirements, they will be presumptively approvable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of rural electric cooperatives and subcategories for small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA solicited comment on potential exclusions or subcategories for small entities based on class, type, or size of source and whether rural electric cooperatives and small utility distribution systems (serving 50,000 customers or less) can expect access to hydrogen and CCS infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether subcategories or exclusions are warranted for rural cooperatives or small utilities based on infrastructure access, costs, and consistency with the Clean Air Act; document rationale for decision (EPA determined separate subcategory for rural cooperatives not warranted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-GHG hydrogen BSER pathway not finalized due to cost/availability concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not finalizing the low-GHG hydrogen BSER pathway. Additional analysis led EPA to assess that the cost of low-GHG hydrogen in 2030 will likely be higher than proposed, and these higher cost estimates and uncertainties regarding nationwide availability were key factors in the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BSER pathways premised on fuels/technologies must be supported by cost and availability analyses; significant uncertainty or higher-than-expected costs can preclude finalizing a pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCS BSER considerations (geographic availability, timelines, materials, workforce)
rubrics_metrics.description: For CCS, EPA considered geographic availability of sequestration, timelines, materials, and workforce necessary for installing CCS, and determined they are sufficient. BSER is premised on source-to-sink CO2 pipelines and sequestration; many EGUs in rural areas may benefit from existing CCS deployment synergies (e.g., ethanol industry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of CCS as BSER requires analysis of sequestration availability, pipeline infrastructure, timelines, workforce, and potential synergies with other industries; document evidence supporting sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Entity Compliance Guide availability and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is preparing a Small Entity Compliance Guide to help small entities comply with this rule. The guide will be available 60 days after publication of the final rule at the specified EPA webpage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accessible compliance guidance targeted to small entities within a defined timeframe after rule publication and host on agency website.

rubrics_metrics.name: UMRA analysis and $100 million unfunded-mandate threshold application
rubrics_metrics.description: The NSPS contain a Federal mandate under UMRA that may result in expenditures of $100 million or more for the private sector in any one year. The NSPS do not contain an unfunded mandate of $100 million or more for state, local, and tribal governments in the aggregate. EPA prepared, under section 202 of UMRA, a written statement of the benefit-cost analysis. Emission guidelines do not impose direct compliance requirements on regulated entities apart from states developing plans under CAA section 111(d); the burden for states was estimated below $100 million in any one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a rule triggers UMRA unfunded-mandate thresholds for private sector and governments, prepare required written analyses, and report estimated burdens for states; document whether section 203 applies (here determined not to apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with state and local governments (Federalism - E.O. 13132)
rubrics_metrics.description: These actions do not have federalism implications as defined in E.O. 13132. Consistent with cooperative federalism, states will establish standards for existing sources under the emission guidelines. EPA consulted with representatives of state and local governments and invited ten national organizations representing elected state and local officials to a virtual meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When actions implicate state implementation responsibilities, engage in timely consultation with state and local representatives and document outreach and opportunities for meaningful input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation and coordination with Indian tribes (E.O. 13175)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions do not have tribal implications as specified in E.O. 13175 because emission guidelines do not directly impose specific requirements on tribal governments; tribes are not required to develop plans. EPA offered government-to-government consultation and outreach and would consult with affected tribes before developing any standards for sources on tribal land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess tribal implications, offer government-to-government consultation when tribal interests exist, and consult before developing standards that would apply on tribal lands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of children from environmental health risks (E.O. 13045) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is subject to E.O. 13045 because it is a significant regulatory action. The Agency evaluated environmental health and welfare effects of climate change on children and found that CO2 emissions reductions resulting from the rule will further improve children's health; cited literature on vulnerabilities of children, elderly, and the poor is used to support analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For significant regulatory actions, evaluate disproportionate risks to children and other vulnerable populations and document expected public health benefits from emission reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy effects analysis (E.O. 13211 and Statement of Energy Effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: These actions are likely to have a significant adverse effect on the supply, distribution or use of energy. EPA prepared a Statement of Energy Effects estimating a 1.4 percent increase in retail electricity prices on average in 2035, a 42 percent reduction in coal-fired electricity generation in 2035, and a 3 percent increase in delivered natural gas prices in 2035. EPA demonstrates compliance can be achieved while maintaining resource adequacy and includes flexibility measures designed to address reliability concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and include an energy effects statement for rules likely to significantly affect energy supply/distribution/use; quantify projected impacts and explain measures to maintain resource adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: NTTAA / 1 CFR part 51 - search for and incorporation of voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: This rulemaking involves technical standards. EPA conducted searches for voluntary consensus standards and, in accordance with 1 CFR part 51, is incorporating by reference 10 voluntary consensus standards (ANSI, ASME, ASTM, ISO standards). No applicable voluntary consensus standards were identified for EPA Method 19 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rule involves technical standards, search relevant standards databases, document results, and incorporate appropriate voluntary consensus standards by reference per 1 CFR part 51; explicitly note any methods for which no VCS exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific consensus standards for monitoring, testing, and fuel definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The preamble lists specific standards and their purposes, e.g., ANSI C12.20-2010 for electricity meters (assure consistent monitoring of electric output used for compliance calculations); ASME PTC 22-2014 for gas turbine thermal performance tests; ASME PTC 46-1996 for overall plant performance tests; ISO 2314:2009 for gas turbine acceptance tests; ASTM standards to define fuel types (coal rank, fuel oils, diesel, kerosene, biodiesel blends).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and apply the referenced consensus standards for measurement, testing, and fuel classification where the regulatory text incorporates them by reference and specifies the sections they apply to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference citations in §60.17
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory text revises §60.17 to add IBR approvals for the listed ANSI, ASME, ASTM, ISO, CSA, EN, and other standards and specifies which sections of part 60 they are IBR-approved for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the Code of Federal Regulations incorporation-by-reference entries accurately list standards, approval dates, and the specific regulatory sections that rely on each standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and purpose of Subpart TTTT (scope and dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart establishes emission standards and compliance schedules for control of GHG emissions from steam generating units or IGCC facilities and stationary combustion turbines that commence construction, reconstruction, or modification within specified date ranges (e.g., after Jan 8, 2014 and on or before May 23, 2023 for certain units).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clearly the unit types and the date windows (construction/reconstruction/modification) to which the subpart applies so regulated entities can determine applicability.
